name: quality-controlled native-event venue latency replication
analysis_status: New exploratory analysis of previously collected and previously studied data; the inherited training/held_out labels do not make this a new preregistered confirmation.
matching_definition: For each valid bid/ask change, find the first strictly later follower quote at or beyond the new price in the direction of the change. An equal-time follower already at the price is already, not a positive-latency match. Later leader reversals do not cancel an event.
quality_policy: Integer nanodollar prices and nanosecond clocks; F_LAST completed states only; snapshots, bad receive timestamps, maybe-bad-book flags, missing/nonpositive/locked/crossed quotes, conflicting same-clock states, per-symbol clock reversals, and quote ages above the threshold are observation barriers. Matches never cross barriers in either venue.
cohort_policy: Primary horizon-specific match rates and conditional matched-latency quantiles require the entire horizon observable in both venues, including for early matches. Already/no-prior-state/quality-truncated/request-end-truncated cases remain separately counted. All-event and bid/ask-stratified counts are retained. Symbols are never pooled for inference.
exchange_clock_boundary_policy: Capture-selected files do not certify exposure to the requested end on each exchange clock. Exchange-clock support ends conservatively at the last retained timestamp or the requested end, whichever is earlier.
volatility_policy: Cross-venue median midpoint on each selected clock with at least half the intended venues observable; full trailing 300 one-second returns required. Retrospective within-date/symbol top-quartile realized volatility defines volatile; first five minutes and incomplete windows remain unknown. This is a descriptive regime label, not an available-ahead-of-time forecasting signal.
inference_estimand: Equal-date mean of conditional per-date pair medians, separately by symbol, clock, horizon and study. Regime contrast pairs calm/volatile medians on the same supported dates. Five-session moving date blocks resample all pairs and stocks together; primary marginal exploratory intervals require all twenty inherited held_out dates supported. No event-independence or familywise significance claim.

source_attribution.contribution: Reaction-latency definition, two-clock comparison, lead-lag/event-study and volatility-regime analysis ideas. Implemented independently inside ColonyLab with additional quality and inference controls.

limitations: Price matching and predictive ordering do not identify causal propagation or pure exchange infrastructure latency.
Conditional medians omit fully observed events that never reach the price within the horizon; match rates and restricted mean waiting times must accompany them.
The available MBP-1 windows are thirty minutes on forty dates and ten minutes on ten other dates, not complete trading sessions.
IEX is absent from these saved MBP-1 studies. No new data is downloaded.
The hundred-millisecond MBO grid and midpoint-only jump caches cannot recover event-level bid/ask latency and are not substituted for native quotes.
Feed flags and source hash checks cannot certify unreported upstream completeness; no saved date-level provider-condition catalogue covers these MBP-1 dates.
Twenty dates contain about four non-overlapping five-session blocks; intervals are approximate. Multiple pairwise intervals are exploratory.
The 250-millisecond quote-age rule preserves the earlier partial-window MBP network convention; quiet initialized full-stream books can remain valid for longer.
